isolationStep.para: This data module provides systematic fault isolation procedures for the speech communications system (ATA 23-10). Use this procedure when system malfunctions are reported or detected during operational testing.

isolationStep.title: Initial Fault Verification
isolationStep.para: Before proceeding with detailed troubleshooting, verify the fault condition:
Obtain detailed description of malfunction from flight crew or maintenance report.
Attempt to reproduce fault condition using normal system operation or test procedure (DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-300A).
Check maintenance history for recent work on communications system that may be related.
Verify aircraft power systems are operating normally (battery voltage, electrical bus status).

isolationStep.title: Fault Category Determination
isolationStep.para: Classify the fault into one of the following categories to direct troubleshooting:
Category 1: No power / Complete system failure
Category 2: No transmit capability
Category 3: No receive capability
Category 4: Degraded audio quality
Category 5: Intermittent operation
Category 6: Display or control malfunction

isolationStep.title: Category 1: No Power / Complete System Failure
isolationStep.para: System completely inoperative, no display illumination, no audio.
Check circuit breakers for communications system:
Visually inspect circuit breakers - verify none are tripped (popped out).
If breaker tripped, investigate cause before resetting. Do not repeatedly reset tripped breaker.
If breaker OK, proceed to next step.
Verify aircraft main electrical power:
Check battery voltage - must be minimum 24V DC for 28V system.
Verify electrical bus voltages using multimeter or system display.
If power system fault found, resolve electrical issue first before continuing communications troubleshooting.
Check power connections at radio unit:
Access avionics bay and locate VHF radio unit.
Verify power connector is fully seated and locked.
Measure voltage at radio power pins (refer to wiring diagram for pin identification).
If no voltage present at radio connector, trace wiring back to source - check for open circuit, damaged wiring, or faulty connections.
If power is present but radio does not operate:
Check radio unit master ON/OFF switch position.
Verify configuration pin settings (if applicable) match installation requirements.
Suspect radio unit internal failure - perform unit substitution test or send unit for bench test.

isolationStep.title: Category 2: No Transmit Capability
isolationStep.para: Radio receives normally but cannot transmit.
Verify PTT (push-to-talk) circuit:
Test PTT button operation - verify button physically actuates with normal force.
Check PTT wiring from control yoke or microphone to radio unit.
Measure continuity of PTT circuit when button pressed (circuit should close to ground).
If PTT circuit OK, proceed to next step.
Check transmitter selection on audio control panel:
Verify correct radio (VHF-1 or VHF-2) is selected for transmission.
Confirm transmit indicator illuminates on audio panel when PTT pressed.
Test alternate transmitter selection to isolate audio panel vs. radio issue.
Verify microphone operation:
Test with alternate known-good microphone or headset.
Check microphone connector for damage or contamination.
Measure microphone impedance (typically 150-600 ohms depending on type).
Check antenna system:
Visually inspect VHF antenna for physical damage.
Measure antenna VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) with appropriate test equipment - should be <2.0:1 across VHF band.
Verify antenna cable connections are tight and corrosion-free.
If all external components check OK, suspect radio transmitter fault - replace radio unit.

isolationStep.title: Category 3: No Receive Capability
isolationStep.para: Radio transmits normally but cannot receive.
Verify receiver audio path:
Check volume control setting - ensure not set to minimum.
Verify audio source selection on audio panel - ensure VHF radio is enabled for reception.
Test headset/speaker output with alternate audio source (marker beacon, intercom) to verify audio system functional.
Check squelch setting:
Rotate squelch control to minimum position.
Background noise should be audible if squelch is functioning correctly.
If no noise audible even with squelch at minimum, suspect receiver fault.
Verify antenna system (same checks as transmit troubleshooting above).
Test receiver sensitivity:
Tune to frequency with known strong signal (ATIS, tower at nearby airport).
If strong signals not received, suspect receiver fault - replace radio unit.

isolationStep.title: Category 4: Degraded Audio Quality
isolationStep.para: Communications functional but audio is distorted, weak, or noisy.
Check all audio connections:
Verify headset connector fully seated and locked.
Inspect connectors for bent pins, corrosion, or foreign material.
Clean connectors with approved contact cleaner if contamination present.
Test with alternate headset to eliminate headset as cause.
Check for sources of electrical interference:
Note if noise is present during all flight phases or only when certain equipment operating.
Systematically disable other avionics to identify interference source.
Verify all equipment properly grounded and shielded.
Adjust audio levels and squelch for optimal clarity.
If audio issues persist and are present on multiple frequencies with different ground stations, suspect radio internal audio circuitry fault.

isolationStep.title: Category 5: Intermittent Operation
isolationStep.para: System operates normally at times but fails unpredictably.
Attempt to identify pattern or trigger:
Note environmental conditions when fault occurs (temperature, vibration, altitude).
Check if fault correlates with operation of other equipment.
Record whether fault is consistent or truly random.
Inspect all connections for intermittent contact:
Exercise connectors by disconnecting and reconnecting while monitoring system.
Check connector locking mechanisms - verify positive retention.
Inspect wiring for chafing, stress, or movement that could cause intermittent opens.
Perform thermal stress test:
Operate system in both hot and cold conditions to provoke temperature-sensitive faults.
Use heat gun (carefully) or cold spray on suspect components while monitoring operation.
Vibration test:
Gently tap on radio unit and connectors while system operating to detect vibration-sensitive faults.
Intermittent faults are difficult to isolate. If fault cannot be consistently reproduced, consider operational monitoring and data logging to capture fault conditions for analysis.

isolationStep.title: Category 6: Display or Control Malfunction
isolationStep.para: Radio operates but display or controls do not function properly.
Verify display illumination and readability:
Check panel lighting control setting - verify not set too dim.
Observe display from different viewing angles to detect LCD polarization issues.
Test control knobs and buttons:
Verify mechanical operation of each control - should rotate or actuate smoothly with proper tactile feedback.
Check if control inputs are recognized by observing system response.
Perform control head self-test if available (press and hold TEST button during power-up).
If display or controls malfunctioning, suspect control head unit failure - replace unit.

isolationStep.title: BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) Codes
isolationStep.para: If radio displays fault codes, refer to the following common BITE codes:
Code E01: Transmitter power output low - Check antenna system, if OK replace radio.
Code E02: Receiver sensitivity degraded - Replace radio unit.
Code E03: Frequency synthesizer fault - Replace radio unit.
Code E04: Internal power supply fault - Check input voltage, if OK replace radio.
Code E05: Memory/configuration error - Perform software reload (DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-C40A), if fault persists replace radio.

isolationStep.title: Component Replacement Procedures
isolationStep.para: When fault isolation determines component replacement necessary:
For audio panel removal: Refer to DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-520A
For audio panel installation: Refer to DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-620A
After component replacement, perform operational test per DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-300A to verify fault resolution.
Record all troubleshooting steps performed in aircraft maintenance log.
Document fault symptoms, tests performed, and corrective actions taken.
If components replaced, record old unit serial number and new unit serial number.
Tag removed components with failure description for warranty or repair processing.
